clue.text: Writer dies getting arrangement sanctioned

parts.note: a writer is an author

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word dies sets its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A writer dies after getting a deal officially approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dies' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is the raw material that 'arrangement' reorders.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sanctioned has been given official permission or approval.

clue.text: Result of an Apollo mission?

parts.note: an outcome in general, but read literally a rocket fired skyward on a moon flight

explanation.surface: A question about what a space flight achieved.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome or conclusion is the final result of events.

clue.text: Principal record produced, by singer, perhaps

parts.note: a principal of a school is its head
a singer produces a musical note, among other sounds

explanation.surface: A lead recording is made by a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A headnote is a summary placed at the top of a law report or document, a written record.

clue.text: King's no rising novelist

parts.note: Richard is a royal name, so a king's possession is Richard's

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word no is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A monarch is not climbing in the world, says a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Richardson was an 18th-century English writer of Pamela and Clarissa.

clue.text: Surprise some of the most artless.

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Even the most naive people can be taken aback.
explanation.definitionFit: To surprise someone is to make them jump with shock.

clue.text: Periods of bewilderment, say ?

indicators.note: say signals that the word for bewilderment is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: a daze is a state of bewilderment

explanation.surface: Times of confusion, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Days are units of time, periods of twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Game is at one-change outside

indicators.note: outside says the coins go round the other letters

parts.note: pence are coins, small change
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A game is in unison, with money on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is a card game for one player, called solitaire in America.

clue.text: Call the Führer the first mischief-maker

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
Führer is German for leader

explanation.surface: Telephoning Hitler is the first act of a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader heads a group causing trouble, its chief instigator.

clue.text: African soldier, king in an oriental garment

parts.note: the article an gives the single letter A

indicators.note: in says the king's letter goes inside the garment

parts.note: a sari is the wrapped dress worn in India
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king is pictured wearing an Eastern robe beside an African soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An askari was a local soldier serving in a colonial army in East Africa.

clue.text: Note unusual antics by a cattle farm

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes

indicators.note: unusual suggests the word antics is put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on strange goings-on at a ranch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a verb, 'remark on', but it is the musical letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: An estancia is a large ranch in Spanish-speaking South America, where cattle are raised.

clue.text: Quietly stealing out of No 10?

parts.note: seems to be about slipping away from Downing Street, but No 10 is the cattle farm at 10 across, and the theft is of its livestock

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks out of the Prime Minister's residence at 10 Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 looks like Downing Street, the British Prime Minister's home, but it is the 10-across answer, a cattle ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustling is the stealing of cattle or horses, and it also names a soft whispering noise.

clue.text: Collection of books initially given to an emperor

indicators.note: initially puts the collection of books first, ahead of the next piece

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A library is handed over to a ruler at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors, such as Otto the Great.

clue.text: Only a girl I embarrassed, in the beginning

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests the words only a girl I are flustered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they once embarrassed nobody but a single girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally means at first, at the outset.

clue.text: What men are loth to show

definitions.text: What men are loth to show

parts.words: What men are loth to show
parts.note: seems to be about something men hide, such as feelings, but read literally it is the quality of being loth itself

explanation.surface: A remark about the emotions men keep hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Being loth means being unwilling, and unwillingness shown is a hesitancy to act.

clue.text: Dismissal connected with backwardness in language that's innate

parts.note: a congé is a formal dismissal

indicators.note: backwardness in says the language name is written in reverse

parts.note: Latin is a language

explanation.surface: Being sacked is linked to slowness with words, which is inborn.
explanation.walkthrough: The dismissal word is a French borrowing, congé, written without its accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A congenital condition is present from birth, inborn.

clue.text: Anger-or the odour of sanctity?

definitions.meaning: the perfumed smoke burnt in church services

explanation.surface: Rage set against the holy smell of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage is to infuriate; and the fragrant resin burnt during worship gives churches their smell of holiness.

clue.text: Clergyman mountain-climbing in range

indicators.note: in says the mountain goes inside the range

parts.note: a chain is a range of mountains

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the mountain is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A priest goes mountaineering in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a minister attached to a regiment, hospital or college.

clue.text: Aid sent possibly as an alternative

indicators.note: possibly says the words aid sent could be formed differently

explanation.surface: Relief is dispatched perhaps as a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one thing rather than another is doing it as a substitute.

clue.text: Winding about through a sort of trout and duck country

indicators.note: a sort of says the letters of trout form a different version

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A river meanders through fish and duck territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges TROUT into TORTU.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortuous road is full of twists and bends.

clue.text: Confounded axe-head struck hard

indicators.note: head of the word axe means its first letter

parts.note: to bash something is to strike it hard

explanation.surface: An axe-head hit violently is ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abashed is embarrassed and disconcerted.

clue.text: Could be thought of one man without spirit — Jack

annotationWithheld.why: Could be thought of one man without spirit — Jack (10): I + MA + GIN + ABLE fits the answer, but no reading of 'man without spirit' and 'Jack' gives MAGIN and ABLE without sharing a letter or stretching Jack to ABLE
annotationWithheld.clue: Could be thought of one man without spirit — Jack

clue.text: Bring up, as the Duke of Flaza-Toro did this

definitions.text: as the Duke of Flaza-Toro did this
definitions.meaning: the Duke led his regiment from behind, so he brought up the back of the column

explanation.surface: Raising a family compared with a comic duke's habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Plaza-Toro (printed Flaza-Toro) is from Gilbert and Sullivan's The Gondoliers; he 'led his regiment from behind'.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise children is to nurture them; and bringing up the back is being at the back of the column.

clue.text: Old coin given to a girl

parts.note: an angel was an old English gold coin

explanation.surface: An antique coin is presented to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela is a woman's name.

clue.text: On which we are exactly like quadrupeds

definitions.text: On which we are exactly like quadrupeds

parts.words: On which we are exactly like quadrupeds
parts.note: the posture on hands and knees, in which a person stands like a four-legged animal

explanation.surface: A remark about when people resemble animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawling on hands and knees puts a person on four limbs, like a beast.

clue.text: Heavenly example of Kipling's female of the species

definitions.text: Heavenly example of Kipling's female of the species

parts.words: Heavenly example of Kipling's female of the species
parts.note: Kipling's poem The Female of the Species calls her more deadly than the male; the she-bear is his first example, and a she-bear is a constellation in the sky

explanation.surface: A celestial instance of the dangerous female in Kipling's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem opens with the she-bear as the female deadlier than the male; Ursa Major, the Great Bear, is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa is Latin for she-bear and names the Great and Little Bear star groups.

clue.text: Do gnomes need asbestos gloves for this?

definitions.text: Do gnomes need asbestos gloves for this?

parts.words: Do gnomes need asbestos gloves for this?
parts.note: the gnomes of Zurich are Swiss bankers, and funds moving fast between markets would, taken literally, burn their hands

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about garden gnomes handling something scorching.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'gnomes of Zurich' was a 1960s British jibe at Swiss bankers.
explanation.definitionFit: Speculative capital moved rapidly between countries for quick profit is called this.

clue.text: Fats engulfing one of Scotland's gentry

indicators.note: engulfing says the fats swallow up the next piece

parts.note: lards are cooking fats
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Grease swamps a member of the Scottish upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish landowner, so lairds are the landed gentry of Scotland.

clue.text: Spaniard writes articles about Laud — is eccentric

indicators.note: about says the two articles go round the other letters

parts.note: an is an indefinite article, taken twice for the plural

indicators.note: eccentric says the letters of Laud is are set in an odd order

explanation.surface: A Spaniard writes pieces about Archbishop Laud, who is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: William Laud was a 17th-century Archbishop of Canterbury; 'writes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Andalusian comes from Andalusia, the southern region of Spain.
